claims.claim: A middleware takes a state creator and returns a new state creator.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/immer.ts:73 `(initializer) => (set, get, store) => ...`; src/middleware/persist.ts:187; src/middleware/devtools.ts:188-190; src/middleware/subscribeWithSelector.ts:47; src/middleware/ssrSafe.ts:12-15; src/middleware/combine.ts:12-14 all accept a StateCreator and return one.
claims.note: Not universal: redux takes (reducer, initialState) rather than a creator (src/middleware/redux.ts:39) though it still returns a StateCreator; the course covers redux separately.

claims.claim: Inside, a middleware receives (set, get, api).
claims.evidence: src/vanilla.ts:33-37 StateCreator signature (setState, getState, store); src/vanilla.ts:95 `createState(setState, getState, api)`.

claims.claim: Middleware typically wraps set and/or patches methods on api.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/immer.ts:76 (store.setState =), persist.ts:231 (api.setState =) and :337 (api.persist =), devtools.ts:216 (api.setState =) and :246 (api.devtools =), subscribeWithSelector.ts:51 (api.subscribe =), ssrSafe.ts:22 (api.setState =), redux.ts:42 (api.dispatch =).

claims.claim: combine wraps none of set, get or api.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/combine.ts:14 `(...args) => Object.assign({}, initialState, create(...args))` forwards the args untouched and mutates nothing on the api.

claims.claim: combine merges an initial state object in front of the creator's result.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/combine.ts:14 `Object.assign({}, initialState, (create as any)(...args))`.
claims.note: Argument order means the creator's result overrides initialState on key collision (type Write<T,U> = Omit<T, keyof U> & U at combine.ts:3,13).

claims.claim: combine infers the types for you.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/combine.ts:5-13 generics T and U are inferred from the two arguments; docs/reference/middlewares/combine.md:10-15 'automatically infers types ... making curried version of create ... not necessary'.

claims.claim: immer assigns store.setState and runs function updaters through produce.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/immer.ts:76-82 `store.setState = (updater, replace, ...args) => { const nextState = typeof updater === 'function' ? produce(updater) : updater; return set(nextState, replace, ...args) }`; :84 passes store.setState to the initializer as its set.

claims.claim: persist reassigns api.setState so that storage is written after each change.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:229-234 `savedSetState = api.setState; api.setState = (state, replace) => { savedSetState(state, replace); return setItem() }`; setItem at :221-227.

claims.claim: devtools reassigns api.setState so that each change is reported to the extension.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/devtools.ts:216-245 `api.setState = ((state, replace, nameOrAction) => { const r = set(state, replace); ... connection?.send(action, get()) ...})`.
claims.note: Only on the active path: with no extension or enabled=false it returns `fn(set, get, api)` untouched (devtools.ts:208-210); reporting is skipped while recording is paused (:218, :416).

claims.claim: ssrSafe swaps in a throwing setter on the server, patching api.setState too.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/ssrSafe.ts:13 `isSSR = typeof window === 'undefined'`; :19-23 `ssrSet = () => { throw new Error('Cannot set state of Zustand store in SSR') }; api.setState = ssrSet; return config(ssrSet, get, api)`.
claims.note: Exported publicly as `unstable_ssrSafe` and marked experimental (src/middleware.ts:17; ssrSafe.ts:3-5).

claims.claim: When persist finds no storage it wraps set with a warning and leaves api.setState alone (src/middleware/persist.ts:208-219).
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:208-219 `if (!storage) { return config((...args) => { console.warn(...); set(...args) }, get, api) }` returns before the api.setState reassignment at :231.

claims.claim: That no-storage branch is the one exception where a shipped middleware wraps set without patching api.setState.
claims.evidence: All seven middleware read in full: combine.ts:14 and subscribeWithSelector.ts:69 and redux.ts:39-48 do not wrap set; immer.ts:76-84, persist.ts:231-243, devtools.ts:216/265, ssrSafe.ts:22-23 wrap set AND patch api.setState; only persist.ts:208-219 wraps set alone.

claims.claim: subscribeWithSelector overwrites api.subscribe.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/subscribeWithSelector.ts:50-51 `const origSubscribe = api.subscribe; api.subscribe = ((selector, optListener, options) => {...})`.

claims.claim: persist adds api.persist.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:337-369 `(api as ...).persist = { setOptions, clearStorage, getOptions, rehydrate, hasHydrated, onHydrate, onFinishHydration }`.
claims.note: The course's api-patch inventory omits that persist also reassigns api.getInitialState (persist.ts:245) and that devtools wraps api.dispatch when redux is present (devtools.ts:282-299).

claims.claim: devtools adds api.devtools.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/devtools.ts:246-256 `(api as ...).devtools = { cleanup: () => {...} }`.

claims.claim: redux attaches a dispatch to the api.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/redux.ts:42-45 `(api as any).dispatch = (action) => { set((state) => reducer(state, action), false, action); return action }`; :46 also sets api.dispatchFromDevtools = true.

claims.claim: get reaches every middleware but none of the built-ins wrap it (wrapping get is an unused extension point).
claims.evidence: get is forwarded unchanged: combine.ts:14 (...args), immer.ts:84, persist.ts:216 and :241, devtools.ts:209 and :265, subscribeWithSelector.ts:69, ssrSafe.ts:17 and :23; redux.ts:39 receives it as `_get` and ignores it. No middleware file reassigns api.getState (persist.ts:245 reassigns getInitialState only).
claims.note: Asserted in both mc-shape-b3 and mc-arch-b0; checked once.

claims.claim: persist wraps set to write the partialized state to storage after each change.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:236-243 creator receives `(...args) => { set(...args); return setItem() }`; :221-227 setItem writes `options.partialize({ ...get() })` with version under options.name.
claims.note: setItem runs after every set call, including ones vanilla treats as no-ops (Object.is-equal state).

claims.claim: On creation persist reads storage.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:371-373 `if (!options.skipHydration) hydrate()` runs synchronously inside the creator; :270 `toThenable(storage.getItem.bind(storage))(options.name)`.

claims.claim: persist runs a version check and migrate on the stored value.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:273-289: if stored version is a number and differs from options.version, calls options.migrate(state, version) (sync or Promise); without migrate it console.errors and the stored state is discarded (falls to :294 `[false, undefined]`).

claims.claim: persist shallow-merges the stored state over the initial state.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:193-196 default `merge: (persistedState, currentState) => ({ ...currentState, ...persistedState })`; :302-305 `options.merge(migratedState, get() ?? configResult)`; :307 `set(stateFromStorage, true)`.
claims.note: For synchronous storage get() is still undefined during creation so the base is configResult (the initial state). For async storage the merge runs when the read resolves, over whatever get() returns then (current state).

claims.claim: Storage defaults to localStorage via createJSONStorage.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:190 `storage: createJSONStorage<S, void>(() => window.localStorage)`; JSDoc :76 `@default createJSONStorage(() => window.localStorage)`; docs/reference/middlewares/persist.md:54.

claims.claim: The default merge is a shallow merge of persisted state over current state.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:108-110 JSDoc 'By default, this function does a shallow merge'; :193-196 object-spread implementation; docs/reference/middlewares/persist.md:70-71 'Defaults to a shallow merge'.

claims.claim: If a new release adds a nested field, the persisted blob can overwrite the whole nested object and drop the new defaults.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:193-196: a top-level key present in persistedState replaces the current key wholesale (object spread, no recursion). docs/reference/middlewares/persist.md:710-731,756 walk through exactly this case (stored `{ position: { y: 100 } }` missing `x`, fixed with a deepMerge `merge`).

claims.claim: Pass a custom merge (or migrate) when the state shape changes.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:93-110 `version`, `migrate`, `merge` options; docs/reference/middlewares/persist.md:66-71, migrate example :588-600, custom merge :756.

claims.claim: The redux middleware wires a reducer plus initial state.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/redux.ts:39 `(reducer, initial) => (set, _get, api) => ...`; :43 `set((state) => reducer(state, action), false, action)`; :48 returns `{ dispatch, ...initial }`.

claims.claim: redux attaches dispatch to both the state and the api.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/redux.ts:42 `(api as any).dispatch = ...` and :48 `return { dispatch: (...args) => (api as any).dispatch(...args), ...initial }`.

claims.claim: devtools connects the store to the Redux DevTools extension.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/devtools.ts:200-203 reads `window.__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION__`; :141 and :149 `extensionConnector.connect(options)`; :267/:270 `connection.init(...)`.

claims.claim: devtools labels each change as an action.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/devtools.ts:219-229 builds `{ type: anonymousActionType || findCallerName(stack) || 'anonymous' }` or `{ type: nameOrAction }`; :231 and :234-243 `connection.send(action, state)`.

claims.claim: devtools replaces api.setState with a three-argument version that also reports to the extension.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/devtools.ts:216 `api.setState = ((state, replace, nameOrAction: Action) => ...)`; type at :76-77 `setState(...args: [...TakeTwo<Sa1>, action?: Action])`; vanilla setState has two params (src/vanilla.ts:1-7).

claims.claim: devtools subscribes to the extension.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/devtools.ts:301-308 `(connection as ...).subscribe((message) => { switch (message.type) ... })`.

claims.claim: RESET, ROLLBACK, JUMP_TO_STATE / JUMP_TO_ACTION and IMPORT_STATE write state back into the store through setStateFromDevtools.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/devtools.ts:359 RESET, :375/:379 ROLLBACK, :383-396 JUMP_TO_STATE/JUMP_TO_ACTION (:387, :394), :404/:406 IMPORT_STATE all call setStateFromDevtools; defined :258-263 as raw `set(...)` with recording paused.
claims.note: The `__setState` ACTION path (:322, :345) also writes back; COMMIT and PAUSE_RECORDING do not.

claims.claim: That write-back is what makes time-travel debugging work.
claims.evidence: docs/reference/middlewares/devtools.md:3 'How to time-travel debug your store'; the JUMP_TO_STATE/JUMP_TO_ACTION handlers (src/middleware/devtools.ts:383-396) are the only path by which the extension's history navigation reaches the store.

claims.claim: The README warns that middlewares that modify set or get are not applied to getState and setState.
claims.evidence: README.md:250 ':warning: Note that middlewares that modify `set` or `get` are not applied to `getState` and `setState`.' (verbatim).

claims.claim: If a middleware wraps only the set argument and never reassigns api.setState, the raw api bypasses the wrapper.
claims.evidence: src/vanilla.ts:94-95 the api object holds the raw setState closure and the creator merely receives it as an argument, so a wrapper around the argument is invisible to api.setState unless reassigned; src/middleware/persist.ts:208-219 is the shipped instance of exactly that.

claims.claim: The shipped middleware do patch api.setState (immer.ts, persist.ts, devtools.ts, ssrSafe.ts).
claims.evidence: src/middleware/immer.ts:76, persist.ts:231, devtools.ts:216, ssrSafe.ts:22.
claims.note: Each on its active path only: persist with a storage, devtools with the extension enabled, ssrSafe when isSSR.

claims.claim: A bare store.setState((s) => { s.count = 10 }) goes through immer's draft handling.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/immer.ts:76-82 reassigns store.setState and routes function updaters through produce; probe `store.setState((s) => { s.count = 10 })` on `createStore<S>()(immer(...))` type-checks with tsc 5.9.3 against src at b57db4f.

claims.claim: The repo's own test asserts the bare store.setState draft behavior (tests/immer.test.tsx).
claims.evidence: tests/immer.test.tsx:64-73 'should work with vanilla createStore': `store.setState((state) => { state.count = 10 })` then `expect(store.getState().count).toBe(10)`.

claims.claim: The docs' logger example patches api.setState alongside the wrapped set (docs/learn/guides/advanced-typescript.md).
claims.evidence: docs/learn/guides/advanced-typescript.md:307-318 defines `loggedSet` and also `const setState = store.setState; store.setState = (...a) => { setState(...a); console.log(...) }`, then `return f(loggedSet, get, store)`.

claims.claim: The docs patch api.setState in the logger example 'for exactly this reason' (the raw-api bypass).
claims.evidence: docs/learn/guides/advanced-typescript.md:288-335: the recipe contains no comment or prose explaining why store.setState is patched; the README warning (README.md:250) is in a different document and is not cross-referenced.
claims.note: The mechanics are supported; the attributed motive is the course's inference, not stated by the docs.

claims.claim: The README 'TypeScript Usage' section says to write create<State>()(...) with the extra empty ().
claims.evidence: README.md:467-469 '## TypeScript Usage ... writing `create<State>()(...)` instead of `create(...)`'; example :481 `create<BearState>()(devtools(persist(...)))`.

claims.claim: The first call is where you annotate the state type.
claims.evidence: src/react.ts:48 `<T>(): <Mos extends [...] = []>(initializer: StateCreator<T, [], Mos>) => ...`; same overload in src/vanilla.ts:48-50.

claims.claim: The docs explain the state type cannot be inferred because the state generic is invariant.
claims.evidence: docs/learn/guides/advanced-typescript.md:29 'TLDR: Because state generic `T` is invariant.'; :46-49 covariant-and-contravariant explanation ending 'TypeScript will be unable to infer it'.

claims.claim: The second call lets TypeScript infer the rest, chiefly the middleware mutator list.
claims.evidence: src/react.ts:48-50 the returned function's own generic `Mos` is inferred from the initializer; probe `create<BearState>()(devtools(persist(...)))` type-checks with tsc 5.9.3 against src at b57db4f; tests/middlewareTypes.test.tsx:61,154,224 use the same form.

claims.claim: The reason is that generic inference is all-or-nothing (docs 'Why the currying').
claims.evidence: docs/learn/guides/advanced-typescript.md:92 `<summary>Why the currying ()(...)?</summary>`; :111 'You can either pass all generics or none.'
claims.note: 'all-or-nothing' is the course's paraphrase; the doc's wording is 'all generics or none' and it cites microsoft/TypeScript#10571 (:96).

claims.claim: Without middleware, plain create<State>((set) => ...) types fine.
claims.evidence: src/react.ts:45-47 non-curried overload `<T, Mos ... = []>(initializer: StateCreator<T, [], Mos>)`; probe `create<BearState>((set) => ({...}))` compiled with no error under tsc 5.9.3 against src at b57db4f.

claims.claim: The repo's own tests use the plain non-curried create<State>((set) => ...) form.
claims.evidence: tests/basic.test.tsx:51,72,132,167,443 `create<CounterState>((set) => ({`; tests/types.test.tsx:41,112; tests/middlewareTypes.test.tsx:42.

claims.claim: create<State>(devtools(persist(...))) with only State given fails because the mutator list defaults to [] and the middleware types no longer line up.
claims.evidence: src/react.ts:45 `<T, Mos extends [StoreMutatorIdentifier, unknown][] = []>` (explicit T disables inference of Mos, which takes its default). Direct probe, tsc 5.9.3 against src at b57db4f: error TS2379 'Argument of type StateCreator<BearState, [], [[zustand/devtools, never], [zustand/persist, BearState]], BearState> is not assignable to parameter of type StateCreator<BearState, [], []> ... Type [[zustand/devtools, never], [zustand/persist, BearState]] is not assignable to type [] ... Source has 2 element(s) but target allows only 0.'
claims.note: Side finding, not a course claim: the docs' own non-curried example (docs/learn/guides/advanced-typescript.md:400-411) lists the mutators as [persist, devtools]; in the same probe that order fails and [devtools, persist] compiles.

claims.claim: The vanilla core is the foundation and React, traditional (equality-fn) and the middleware build on it.
claims.evidence: src/react.ts:2 and src/traditional.ts:3 `import { createStore } from './vanilla.ts'`; traditional.ts:21,82 are the equality-fn bindings; every middleware imports StateCreator/StoreApi/StoreMutatorIdentifier from '../vanilla.ts' and augments StoreMutators (immer.ts:3,14-19; persist.ts:1-5,388-392; devtools.ts:3-7,15-20; redux.ts:1,28-32; subscribeWithSelector.ts:1,21-26; combine.ts:1; ssrSafe.ts:1).
claims.note: The middleware imports are type-only (`import type`), so at runtime middleware depends on the api object handed to it, not on the vanilla module.

claims.claim: src/vanilla/shallow.ts imports nothing.
claims.evidence: src/vanilla/shallow.ts:1-74 contains no import statements.

claims.claim: src/react/shallow.ts imports only React and shallow.
claims.evidence: src/react/shallow.ts:1 `import React from 'react'`; :2 `import { shallow } from '../vanilla/shallow.ts'`; no other imports.

claims.claim: shallow/useShallow plug into selection alongside the core without depending on it.
claims.evidence: src/shallow.ts:1-2 only re-exports; neither src/vanilla/shallow.ts nor src/react/shallow.ts imports vanilla.ts or react.ts; useShallow wraps a selector (src/react/shallow.ts:4-12) that is handed to useStore.

claims.claim: The vanilla core has no React dependency.
claims.evidence: src/vanilla.ts:1-100 contains no import statements at all.

claims.claim: React bindings and the equality-fn bindings both wrap createStore.
claims.evidence: src/react.ts:54 `const api = createStore(createState)`; src/traditional.ts:70 `const api = createStore(createState)`.

claims.claim: For zustand/traditional the use-sync-external-store shim is an external dependency.
claims.evidence: src/traditional.ts:2 `import useSyncExternalStoreExports from 'use-sync-external-store/shim/with-selector'`; src/react.ts:30 uses React.useSyncExternalStore directly, so the shim is traditional-only; rollup.config.mjs:18-20 treats every non-relative id as external.

claims.claim: Immer is the external for the immer middleware.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/immer.ts:1 `import { produce } from 'immer'`; package.json:161 peer dependency.

claims.claim: A storage backend is the external for persist.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/persist.ts:7-24 StateStorage/PersistStorage interfaces; :190 default `window.localStorage`.

claims.claim: The Redux DevTools extension is the external for devtools.
claims.evidence: src/middleware/devtools.ts:1 `import type {} from '@redux-devtools/extension'`; :203 `window.__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION__`.

claims.claim: React is an external of the React bindings.
claims.evidence: src/react.ts:1, src/traditional.ts:1, src/react/shallow.ts:1 `import React from 'react'`; package.json:162 peer dependency.

claims.claim: package.json lists react, @types/react, immer and use-sync-external-store as optional peer dependencies.
claims.evidence: package.json:159-164 peerDependencies `@types/react >=18.0.0, immer >=9.0.6, react >=18.0.0, use-sync-external-store >=1.2.0`; :165-178 peerDependenciesMeta marks all four `optional: true`.
